newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - Swissair buys partner's cargo unit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swissair buys partner's cargo unit.

text.p: The cargo division of Swissair is buying the cargo capacity of its Belgian partner Sabena, a Sabena spokesman said on Wednesday.

"Sabena will no longer have a cargo division (and) Swissair's cargo capacity will jump 25 percent," a Sabena spokesman told Reuters. He declined to give financial details of the purchase by Swissair Cargo.

The deal, to be implemented on January 1, 1997, will boost Swissair's cargo capacity to around two billion tonnes per kilometre from 1.6 billion tonnes, strengthening its position as Europe's fifth largest cargo forwarder.
Sabena said in a statement that each company offering freight to Sabena would have access to the entire network of Swissair, which has a 49.5 percent stake in Sabena.
Sabena said Swissair's cargo clients will have access to Sabena's European and African network. Sabena currently flies to 58 European, 22 African and four U.S. destinations plus Tokyo.
Sabena's clients can use Swissair's Asian and North- and South American networks.

The impact of the deal on employment at the two airlines was not immediately known but the Sabena spokesman said most of the 75 jobs in Sabena Cargo's commercial department would be scrapped. "This does not mean they will be sacked," he added.
Sabena has a total workforce of 590 in its cargo division.
The spokesman said the decision, approved last week by Sabena chief executive Paul Reutlinger and Swissair president Philippe Bruggisser, was taken in concert with Sabena trade unions.
"They agreed with the deal, otherwise it would not have been done," he said.

Unions, which have in the past been highly critical of management plans to sell cargo capacity, have been holding talks with management since mid-August on Reutlinger's drastic plan to make the airline profitable again.
Reutlinger said in June Sabena needed to make extra savings of 4.7 billion Belgian francs ($150 million), including two billion francs in labour-related cost reductions between now and 1998.

But Sabena announced earlier this month it had a two billion Belgian francs loss in the first half of 1996, which aviation analysts said raised pressure on unions to comply. Sabena had a 1995 group loss before provisions of 530 million francs.
Sabena will also join Swissair's CARIDO cargo automation system, which Sabena said will be the basis of a new global system for the distribution and upfollowing of shipments. ($1=31.51 Belgian Franc)
